title: Derived germs commute with semilinear transport on a proper geometric fibre
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in the chosen algebraic closure $\Qlb$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. Use the rationalized and common-stage categories of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Let $Y_0$ be proper of finite type over $k_0$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and write $a_Y:Y\to s$. Put $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ and $g=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times h$, where $\gamma=(c\mapsto c^q)^{-1}$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Write $P_r=L(g^r)^*$ and $Q_r=L(h^r)^*$ for derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. All pullback-composition comparisons are the scalar localizations of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], and at $\Qlb$ are represented at a common finite field stage.

For $M\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ put $C(M)=R\Gamma_c(Y,M)$ [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Use the identity compactification of $a_Y$ to identify this with $R\Gamma(Y,M)$ and to form $\tau_{c,M}:C(M)\to C(P_1M)$ [lem-pod-proper-coincidence-frobenius, def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. For a $k$-point $z:s\to Y$ (a geometric point of [def-weil-geometric-point]), put $C_z(M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz^*M)$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Let $e_z^M:C(M)\to C_z(M)$ be the derived germ: through $R\Gamma_c\cong R\Gamma$, it is obtained by applying $\operatorname{Fib}_sLz^*$ to the counit $La_Y^*Ra_{Y*}M\to M$ [fix-prop-adjunctions], using $a_Yz=\operatorname{id}_s$ and the canonical composition comparisons.

For $r\geq1$ let $T(z)=gz h^{-1}$ and $z_r=T^r(z)=g^rz h^{-r}$, which are $k$-points. The equality $g^rz=z_rh^r$ and the specified pullback-composition comparisons give
$$b_{r,z,M}:Q_rLz_r^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Lz^*P_rM.$$
Let $d_r:P_r\xrightarrow{\sim}P_1^{\,r}$ be the iterated composition comparison. Define
$$\tau^{[r]}_{c,M}=C(d_{r,M}^{-1})\circ\tau_{c,P_1^{r-1}M}\circ\cdots\circ\tau_{c,M}:C(M)\longrightarrow C(P_rM).$$
For $N\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ let $I_N^{[r]}:\operatorname{Fib}_s(N)\to\operatorname{Fib}_s(Q_rN)$ be the composite of the $r$ point transports $\iota_N,\iota_{Q_1N},\ldots,\iota_{Q_1^{r-1}N}$ [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], followed by the specified composition comparison.

Then the following identity holds in $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Lambda)$, naturally in $M$, for every $r\geq1$ and every $k$-point $z$:
$$e_z^{P_rM}\circ\tau^{[r]}_{c,M}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(b_{r,z,M})\circ I_{Lz_r^*M}^{[r]}\circ e_{z_r}^M.$$
No Weil structure on $M$ is assumed. In particular the formula concerns the specified exchange-mate/point-transport composite, not an unspecified identification of coefficient spaces.

proof.text: Use the identity compactification throughout. By [lem-pod-proper-coincidence-frobenius](2), the maps $\kappa_M$ identify $C(M)$ with $V R(M)$ and $\tau_{c,M}$ with $\tau_M$, where $R=Ra_{Y*}$ and $V=\operatorname{Fib}_s$. Naturality of $\kappa$ identifies also $C(d_{r,M}^{-1})$ with $VR(d_{r,M}^{-1})$. Thus every arrow in the asserted compact-support formula becomes the corresponding ordinary-cohomology arrow. It suffices to prove that formula for $C=VR$ and $\tau_M=V(E_M)\iota_{RM}$, where $E_M=\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M)$ [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. Properness is used in exactly this reduction; the semilinear maps $g,h$ are still the given scheme automorphisms.

proof.text:
First perform the ordinary calculation on an integral representative $M\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$; passage to the requested coefficients is in step 8. Put $A=La_Y^*$, $P=Lg^*$ and $Q=Lh^*$, and let $\varepsilon:AR\to\mathrm{id}$ be the counit [fix-prop-adjunctions](1). For a $k$-point $x$, write $Z_x=Lx^*$ and let $u_x:Z_xA\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ be the specified pullback comparison for $a_Yx=\mathrm{id}_s$. Define the natural morphism in $D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$
$$v_x^M=Z_x(\varepsilon_M)u_x(RM)^{-1}:RM\longrightarrow Z_xM.$$
By the definition of the germ in the item, its ordinary-cohomology version is $e_x^M=V(v_x^M)$. Naturality follows by applying $Z_x$ to the counit's naturality square and then using naturality of $u_x$. All functors here have the stated bounded constructible domains: $a_Y,x$ are separated finite-type $k$-morphisms, and pullback-composition is [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition].

proof.text:
Let $\theta:AQ\xrightarrow{\sim}PA$ be the pullback comparison for $a_Yg=ha_Y$. The defining exchange mate [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange](1) satisfies
$$(*)\qquad \varepsilon_{PM}\,A(E_M)=P(\varepsilon_M)\theta_{RM}:A Q RM\longrightarrow PM.$$
Indeed, apply [lem-amb-mate-unit-counit] with both adjunctions $A\dashv R$, $G=Q$, $H=P$, and $\alpha=\theta$. For the specified integral exchange, make this calculation on its defining strict coefficient system first: the system adjunction and its actual mate words are supplied by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Apply its specified derived-inverse-limit functor [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] and operation comparisons to the system equality. These comparisons preserve units and counits by [lem-fix-operation-reduction], so the resulting equality is exactly $(*)$ for the completed operations, rather than an equality inferred only from separate reductions. This uses only the ordinary adjunction for the vertical $k$-morphism $a_Y$; it does not apply a $k$-linear base-change theorem to $g$ or $h$.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change (unit-square-counit exchange); Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition. Agent calculation for the specified completed/rational comparisons; transport convention as Deligne Weil II (1.1.7), (1.1.10)-(1.1.14), printed pp. 150-153.

proof.text:
Write $x_1=T(x)$ and $b_M=b_{1,x,M}:QZ_{x_1}M\xrightarrow{\sim}Z_xPM$. Associativity of the specified comparisons [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], applied to $a_Ygx=ha_Yx$ and $gx=x_1h$, gives
$$Z_x(\theta_N)u_x(QN)^{-1}=b_{AN}\,Q(u_{x_1}(N)^{-1}).$$
Both sides expand the comparison from $Q=L(h)^*$ to $Z_xPA$: use $a_Yx=a_Yx_1=\mathrm{id}_s$ and reassociate the three pullbacks; this is the associativity identity of the cited node with the identity factors removed. Apply $Z_x$ to $(*)$ from step 3, precompose with $u_x(QRM)^{-1}$, and use this comparison equality and naturality of $u_x$ and $b$. The resulting calculation is
$$v_x^{PM}E_M=Z_x(P\varepsilon_M)b_{ARM}Q(u_{x_1}(RM)^{-1})
=b_M Q(Z_{x_1}\varepsilon_M)Q(u_{x_1}(RM)^{-1})
=b_M Q(v_{x_1}^M).$$
This is an equality in the derived category on $s$, before evaluating at the point.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change (unit-square-counit exchange); Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition. Agent calculation for the specified completed/rational comparisons; transport convention as Deligne Weil II (1.1.7), (1.1.10)-(1.1.14), printed pp. 150-153.

proof.text:
Apply $V$ to the last equality and precompose with $\iota_{RM}$. Naturality of the specified point transport [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2), applied to the actual derived arrow $v_{x_1}^M:RM\to Z_{x_1}M$, says
$$V(Qv_{x_1}^M)\iota_{RM}=\iota_{Z_{x_1}M}V(v_{x_1}^M).$$
Consequently
$$(**)\qquad e_x^{PM}\tau_M=V(b_{1,x,M})\iota_{Z_{x_1}M}e_{x_1}^M.$$
The arrow $\iota$ here is the restriction--insertion--pullback map of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], not a replacement by an arbitrary isomorphism of vector spaces. Formula $(**)$ holds for every $x$ and every $M$, providing the base case for the iteration.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change (unit-square-counit exchange); Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition. Agent calculation for the specified completed/rational comparisons; transport convention as Deligne Weil II (1.1.7), (1.1.10)-(1.1.14), printed pp. 150-153.

proof.text:
For the induction keep powers uncontracted: put $S_r=P^r$, $J_r=Q^r$, $x_j=T^j(x)$, and let $\widehat\tau_{r,M}$ and $\widehat I_{r,N}$ be the successive $r$ transports, with no final composition comparison. Put $\widehat b_{1,x,M}=b_{1,x,M}$ and recursively
$$\widehat b_{r+1,x,M}=b_{1,x,S_rM}\,Q(\widehat b_{r,x_1,M}):J_{r+1}Z_{x_{r+1}}M\to Z_x S_{r+1}M.$$
Induct on $r\geq1$ to prove
$$e_x^{S_rM}\widehat\tau_{r,M}=V(\widehat b_{r,x,M})\widehat I_{r,Z_{x_r}M}e_{x_r}^M.$$
The case $r=1$ is $(**)$. For $r+1$, apply $(**)$ to $S_rM$ at $x$, and then substitute the inductive formula at $x_1$ for $e_{x_1}^{S_rM}\widehat\tau_{r,M}$. Move $V(\widehat b_{r,x_1,M})$ past the preceding $\iota$ using [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2). The remaining factors are, in order, $V(b_{1,x,S_rM}Q\widehat b_{r,x_1,M})$, $\iota_{J_r Z_{x_{r+1}}M}\widehat I_{r,Z_{x_{r+1}}M}$ and $e_{x_{r+1}}^M$. They are precisely the recursively defined right side at $r+1$.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change (unit-square-counit exchange); Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition. Agent calculation for the specified completed/rational comparisons; transport convention as Deligne Weil II (1.1.7), (1.1.10)-(1.1.14), printed pp. 150-153.

proof.text:
Let $d_r:P_r\xrightarrow{\sim}S_r$ and $f_r:Q_r\xrightarrow{\sim}J_r$ be the specified iterated comparisons. Associativity [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] identifies the recursion of step 6 with the comparison for $g^rx=x_rh^r$:
$$Z_x(d_{r,M}^{-1})\widehat b_{r,x,M}=b_{r,x,M}f_{r,Z_{x_r}M}^{-1}.$$
To check it, expand the recursion into $r$ adjacent squares $gx_j=x_{j+1}h$, then reassociate their pullbacks; both composites are the comparison from $L(g^rx)^*M=L(x_rh^r)^*M$. This is repeated application of the cited associativity identity, starting with equality at $r=1$. By the definitions in the item,
$$\tau_M^{[r]}=VR(d_{r,M}^{-1})\widehat\tau_{r,M},\qquad I_N^{[r]}=V(f_{r,N}^{-1})\widehat I_{r,N}.$$
Naturality of the germ with respect to $d_{r,M}^{-1}:S_rM\to P_rM$ gives $e_x^{P_rM}VR(d_{r,M}^{-1})=V(Z_xd_{r,M}^{-1})e_x^{S_rM}$. Substitute these three equalities into step 6 to obtain exactly
$$e_x^{P_rM}\tau_M^{[r]}=V(b_{r,x,M})I_{Z_{x_r}M}^{[r]}e_{x_r}^M.$$
In this step $\tau$ denotes ordinary transport; step 1 returns this identity to compact support.

proof.text: For $\Lambda=E$, take an integral object representative: [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] has exactly the integral objects and localized Hom groups. Apply the scalar-localization functor to the equality of steps 2--7. The operations, their comparisons, units and counits commute with this passage by [lem-fix-operation-reduction]; the point fiber and point transport are obtained by tensoring the integral fiber and transport with $E$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point, def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. Thus every factor becomes the factor specified in the question, including $b_r,d_r$ and $I^{[r]}$. Naturality holds for localized arrows since the equality is natural in integral arrows and all its factors are $E$-linear. For $\Lambda=\Qlb$, represent $M$ and any morphism used to test naturality over one common finite extension as in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. The already proved equality at that stage gives equality of its two common-stage morphism classes. The same operation comparisons and point-transport naturality [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2) identify the factors after any further coefficient extension, so this is the specified common-stage formula, naturally in $M$. No Weil structure or finite-Tor hypothesis has been used.
